facts.text: Independent assessment is review of safety evidence by people who did not produce it; an independent test body is an outside organization that runs or witnesses tests; a safety board is the internal group authorized to accept or reject the safety case.
facts.quote: Independent assessment is a review of the safety evidence by people who did not produce it; an independent test body is an outside organization that runs or witnesses tests; and a safety board is the internal group with the authority to accept or reject the safety case.

facts.text: Safety-assessment independence can involve a different engineer, a different team, an outside company, or a legally appointed body such as a notified body in the European Union.
facts.quote: Independence comes in degrees: a different engineer, a different team, an outside company, or a body appointed under law such as a notified body in the European Union.

facts.text: Higher required integrity levels entail greater expected independence in safety assessment.
facts.quote: The higher the required integrity level, the more independence is expected [Chapter 12].

facts.text: For most markets, the manufacturer's internal safety board, working under ISO 19014 and ISO 13849, and the customers accept the safety evidence.
facts.quote: For most markets it is the manufacturer's internal safety board, working under ISO 19014 and ISO 13849, plus the customers

facts.text: South African mines check safety evidence against Regulation 8.10 and MOSH requirements, which include independent verification at two readiness gates.
facts.quote: in South Africa the mines check against Regulation 8.10 and the MOSH requirements, which include independent verification at two readiness gates [Chapters 2, 3].

facts.text: A simulation campaign optimized for internal engineering confidence does not necessarily produce a dossier acceptable to an independent safety board, mine customer or regulator.
facts.quote: A simulation campaign optimized for internal engineering confidence "is not necessarily the dossier an independent safety board, mine customer or regulator will accept" [Chapter 2].

facts.text: A safety board expects evidence including the decision and context of use, traceability, criteria declared in advance, independent physical data, a validity envelope, confirmatory tests partly chosen by the assessor, failed tests and their disposition, and a residual-risk statement.
facts.quote: the decision and context of use, traceability, criteria declared in advance, independent physical data, a validity envelope, confirmatory tests some of which the assessor chooses, failed tests and their disposition, and a residual-risk statement [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Model developers should not be the only people deciding whether model discrepancies are acceptable.
facts.quote: Model developers should not be the only people deciding whether discrepancies are acceptable

facts.text: The collision-mitigation validation program should budget for an external assessor early.
facts.quote: an external assessor should be budgeted early [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The booklet did not identify who would assess a simulation-based safety argument under the EU Machinery Regulation or what competence a notified body would need.
facts.quote: The booklet did not find who would assess a simulation-based argument under the EU Machinery Regulation or what competence a notified body would need

facts.text: Agreeing on the assessor for a simulation-based argument under the EU Machinery Regulation and on the assessor's criteria is a prerequisite for the program schedule.
facts.quote: agreeing who that counterpart is, and on their criteria, is itself a prerequisite for the schedule [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Independent review can become the validation program's critical path and cannot rescue incomplete engineering late in the program.
facts.quote: Independent review can become the critical path, and it cannot rescue incomplete engineering late [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The booklet's second program gate requires assessor feedback to have been received.
facts.quote: The booklet's second gate requires assessor feedback to have been received

facts.text: The booklet recommends engaging the assessor before the first program gate.
facts.quote: it advises engaging the assessor before the first gate [Chapter 12].
